newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index in record territory in early trade.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index in record territory in early trade.

text.p: German shares traded in record territory on Wednesday, as a strong close on Wall Street overnight and a strengthening dollar boosted sentiment on the DAX index of 30 blue-chip German shares.
The index, which tracks bourse trade in German equities, was up 8.92 points, or 0.24 percent, at 3,683.28 points, having earlier hit a new record high of 3,695.31 points.
The June DAX future contract was up 13 points at 3,687.

"Wall Street was up yesterday and it looks like we're trying to emulate that good order flow here. This is not a down day and I think it's very possible that we could break 3,700 points today," said a Frankfurt broker.
"There is a lot of merger talk out there today, especially since Roche bought Boehringer Mannheim the other day, and people are looking at the banking sector closely," he said.
One of the main engines behind the advance was the insurance giant Allianz, whose shares rose 5.70 marks, around one and a half percent, to 381.50 marks.
Allianz rose after it said it expected its premium income to rise around 11 percent to around 83 billion marks in 1997 and said it expected moderate double-digit growth in 1997.

Industrial gaint Daimler Benz AG was one of the volume leaders early on and advanced strongly in electronic trade after it said it expected "substantial" increases in 1997 sales and operating profits.
The share rose to a high of 137.45 marks at one point in electronic trade. In bourse trade the share was up 1.10 marks, around 0.80 percent, at 137.50 marks.
"The Daimler sales figures for the first four months did not disappoint and were well received," a trader said.
